title: Ravi Kishan Plays Lord Ram for First Time at Delhi Ramleela, Photos Go Viral
excerpt: The actor-MP, who played Sita, Parshuram and Kevat as a child in Ayodhya, took the Ram role at Ayodhya Ki Ramleela for Dussehra and urged youth toward spirituality.
body:
• Actor and BJP MP Ravi Kishan played Lord Ram for the first time at Delhi's Ayodhya Ki Ramleela during Dussehra, in traditional warrior attire with bow and arrow — photos he shared on X went viral.
  • Kishan said his Ramleela journey began in Ayodhya as a child, when he played Parshuram, Kevat and Sita — but never Ram until now.
  • He urged young people to read about Ram, Krishna and Shiva and to use spirituality and meditation to get through depression and difficulty.
  • For diaspora readers: Ramleela clips and photos are circulating on X from his verified handle @ravikishann — the primary source for the viral images.

From playing Sita as a child to playing Ram

Ravi Kishan has waited a lifetime for this role. The actor and BJP MP from Gorakhpur portrayed Lord Ram for the first time at Delhi's Ayodhya Ki Ramleela during Dussehra celebrations, dressed in traditional warrior attire and carrying a bow and arrow, according to ANI reporting carried by the Indian Economic Observer. Photos and video from the stage — including his arrival in a grand chariot — spread quickly online after he shared glimpses on X.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2112582545129054454

"By the grace of Lord Shri Ram, the Ram Lila of Ayodhya was staged in Ram Lila (Delhi). Jai Shri Ram," he wrote on X, in the post that anchored the viral run.

"My journey began with Ramleela"

Kishan traced the moment back to childhood in Ayodhya. "My journey began with Ramleela in Ayodhya, but I had never portrayed Lord Ram before. Today, by the grace of Lord Ram, I am getting the opportunity to take on this role," he said, as reported by The CSR Journal. In childhood performances he had played Parshuram, Kevat and Sita — a detail he repeated to several outlets, framing the Ram role as a closing of a circle rather than a casting novelty.

"Victory to Lord Ram, to Maryada Purushottam, to the best among men. In the same way, we need to destroy the Ravana in our own lives, the Ravana inside us, and the Ravana in society."

— Ravi Kishan, speaking to ANI

That message — Dussehra as the defeat of an inner Ravana as much as the mythological one — was the line he returned to in interview after interview, extending Dussehra wishes and calling for humanity and love to awaken.

A message aimed at young people

Kishan used the attention for a second appeal, directed at youth. "I urge the youth to read about Lord Ram, Lord Krishna and Lord Shiva. Whenever you face depression or difficulties in life, spirituality helps us overcome them. I come from a humble background, and today the world knows me through cinema and as the MP from Gorakhpur," he told media, as reported in coverage of the event by Andhra Vilas. He urged at least half an hour of daily meditation and described Sanatan traditions as a source of strength in hard phases.

The framing fits the festival. Ramleela retells the Ramayana in the run-up to Dussehra and Vijayadashami, marking Ram's victory over Ravana. A sitting MP and film star in the lead role draws crowds and cameras in a way a traditional troupe does not — which is precisely why the images travelled.

On screen next

On the cinema front, ANI noted Kishan was last seen in Mirzapur: The Movie, directed by Gurmmeet Singh alongside Pankaj Tripathi, Divyendu and Ali Fazal. Andhra Vilas reported he will next appear in Khosla Ka Ghosla 2. For diaspora audiences who know him first from Bhojpuri and Hindi cinema, the Ramleela appearance lands differently from a film release: it is unscripted in the public square, in costume, on a religious stage — and, judging by the share counts on his own post, it is the version of Ravi Kishan most people will see this Dussehra.
